instruction.text: Find the car in this image.

feedback.end: Cars are very useful for getting to more remote places, but only people with a driving licence can drive them.

instruction.text: Listen to the statements and decide which one is true.

b.sound: We should always get into a car from the pavement.
We should always get into a car from the road.

feedback.end: Correct! Entering from the pavement means we avoid the cars and bikes on the road.

feedback.finish: Before opening the door of a car, we should always check to make sure we won’t bump into anything or anyone. We don’t want to block a cyclist coming past!

atoms.a: What is this person wearing across their body?

text: When we travel in a car we must always wear a seatbelt to keep us in our seat in the event of a crash.
We should have one strap across our chest and one across our waist, just like the person here.

atoms.a: What safety feature is this person using?

feedback.correct: Childern under the age of 12 and under 135cm tall must use a booster seat or booster cushion so that the seatbelt works properly.
feedback.wrong: A life jacket is used when we are on a boat.

instruction.text: In which image is the person opening their car door correctly?

text: When opening the door to get out of a car, we should use our hand opposite to the door. By using our opposite hand, we are forced to turn and see what is coming, just like this person is doing.

instruction.text: Decide if these statements are true or false.

atoms.a: You must check that nothing is coming before opening the car door.
You don’t always need to wear seatbelts when travelling in the car.
You should always try to enter and exit the car from the pavement.
A booster seat can help your seatbelt to work properly.
